seo.title: Edit table data with Preview SQL and Safe Mode
seo.description: Filter and edit rows, review the SQL before you save, and give each connection a Safe Mode level. Data Rewind puts back the values a save replaced.

header.title: Data editing
header.lead: Filter rows, follow foreign keys and edit values in the grid. Changes wait until you save, with SQL available to review first.

sections.title: Find the rows you need
paragraphs: Sorting and paging run on the server, so a large table opens at its first page. Above {countEstimate} rows the row count is an estimate, with Count Exactly when you need the real number.

blocks.title: Filters and highlight rules
paragraphs: Build filters with {filterOperatorCount} operators or a SQL condition, then save them for reuse. Highlight rules color matching rows or cells and stay on this Mac.

blocks.title: Foreign keys and JSON
paragraphs: Follow a foreign key to its referenced row or preview it in place. A value picker helps you choose from referenced rows. Open JSON values in a tree viewer or text editor.

sections.title: Review edits before saving
paragraphs: Edits, new rows and deletions stay in the tab until you save with <kbd>⌘S</kbd>. <ui>Preview SQL</ui> shows the pending statements. Saving uses bound parameters and checks affected row counts, with a transaction and rollback where the engine supports them.
points: Cell editors for the column’s type: a date and time picker, ENUM and SET lists, arrays, JSON, a hex editor for binary values, and an image viewer.
Undo and redo in each tab until you save.
Query results can be edited when the query reads a single table, with no join, CTE or UNION.
Copy rows as CSV, JSON, Markdown, an IN list, or INSERT and UPDATE statements.

sections.title: Safe Mode
paragraphs: Choose a level per connection: {macSafeModeLevels}. The default is {macSafeModeDefault}, which runs statements without confirmation. Alert confirms writes; Safe Mode adds Touch ID or password approval. Full levels also confirm reads. Read-Only blocks writes and editing. Safe Mode is free.

DROP, TRUNCATE and DELETE without WHERE always require confirmation. Full-window Agent mode enforces at least Alert. Read-only engines and an organization's device-management policy can also raise the effective level.

links.label: Safe Mode and other connection policies

sections.title: Data Rewind
paragraphs: Review and restore values replaced by a save with <ui>Restore Previous Values</ui>. The review flags rows changed since that save. Restores follow Safe Mode, in one transaction where the engine allows.
Previous values stay encrypted on this Mac for {rewindDays} days and never sync. Recording and restoration stop when your paid plan ends.

sections.title: Documents and keys
paragraphs: Edit MongoDB documents as Extended JSON, or rename and remove fields across a collection. On Redis, edit strings, rename keys and set TTLs in the grid, or add a string, hash, list, set or sorted-set key. Use editor commands to change other value types.

sections.title: On iPhone and iPad
paragraphs: Browse rows as cards, sort and filter them, or tap a foreign key to preview its row. Edit values or set NULL; editing and deleting require a primary key. New rows start with DEFAULT values, with NULL and empty string available instead.
Mobile Safe Mode offers {iosSafeModeLevels}, defaulting to {iosSafeModeDefault}. Staged edits, Preview SQL, highlight rules and Data Rewind are currently Mac-only.

limits: Data Rewind is not a backup. It does not undo triggers, cascades or changes made outside TablePro, and it cannot restore rows without a primary key, values over {rewindMaxValue} MB or values the server computed.
An UPDATE without WHERE is an ordinary write: it asks first only at Alert or a stricter level.
On {everyStatementWrites}, Safe Mode counts every statement as a write, so Alert asks before reads too and Read-Only blocks them.
The result of a join, a CTE or a UNION is read-only in the grid; open the table to edit it.
